FILED s532a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-01), found writing ir-spec Â§3.2d's #4086 example.  PRE-EXISTING (base 10cdc985 identical).  A missing die (the program runs on where perl stops).

    eval { for ("lit") { s/x/z/ } }; print "1 ", ($@ ? "died" : "ok"), "\n";   # perl died   PCL ok
    eval { for ("lit") { tr/x/z/ } }; print "2 ", ($@ ? "died" : "ok"), "\n";  # perl died   PCL died
    eval { for ("lit") { s/l/L/ } }; print "3 ", ($@ ? "died" : "ok"), "\n";   # perl died   PCL died

perl's pp_subst checks the target's read-only flag BEFORE it matches (s/// on a constant dies even when nothing would change); tr/// already does.  PCL's s/// only reaches the read-only check on the write.  Layer: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-subst's target write path (the #1391 marked read-only slot).  Probe: scratch/s532a/p/ro.pl in the s532a worktree.
